finding.claim: The /rss endpoint fetches an arbitrary URL taken from the query parameter `u`, with no validation. This is full SSRF. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/, and localhost. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the caller, so the response is partially readable. open-uri also follows redirects, and the ftp scheme is supported as well.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `u` on GET /rss (params[:u], app.rb:8), controlled by any unauthenticated client
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read (app.rb:8), which makes an outbound HTTP/HTTPS/FTP request

trace.note: Route handler for GET /rss, with no authentication
params[:u] is passed straight to URI.open (open-uri) and the body is read
The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the attacker, so this is a non-blind SSRF

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or allowlist check, no private-IP filtering, and no redirect restriction. The TRUSTED allowlist defined at line 5 is not applied to this route. On Ruby 3+, URI.open does not open local files, but it does fetch http, https and ftp URLs.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes unauthenticated params[:u] directly to URI.open(...).read with no validation, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes; the TRUSTED allowlist (app.rb:5) is only enforced in /trusted at app.rb:14, not in /rss.
